page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-192GB is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 16 shared vCPUs and 16 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz, configured with 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is a notable bottleneck, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance ranking in the bottom 10% and single-threaded bzip3 decompression and text processing scoring in the bottom 25%. However, multi-core capabilities are more robust, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and PassMark CPU scores all falling within the average middle 50% range. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also show average performance, though the PassMark memory score is relatively weak, landing in the bottom 25%.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the high memory density, this server offers a cost-effective solution for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous, peak single-core CPU performance. It is well-suited for database operations, caching layers like Redis, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks. It is less suitable for single-threaded applications or heavy large-scale LLM text generation due to poor performance in those specific benchmarks.
